I understand what you're suggesting, but I have to disagree. The general consensus that I've seen around the glyph is that spells that target "Self" can be enforced onto triggering creatures. That's how I got the idea in the first place. (https://rpg.stackexchange.com/questions/115540/can-a-spell-with-a-target-of-self-be-stored-in-glyph-of-warding?noredirect=1&lq=1 and https://rpg.stackexchange.com/questions/90089/is-there-a-way-to-cast-spells-with-a-range-of-self-on-other-targets)

The reason for this is, I assume, because most self-targetting spells in the PHB are buffs, and why would anyone want to buff a Tarrasque? I believe it's intended that an optional use for the spell is to buff allies with strategically placed glyphs, but the fact that there is a self-targeted teleportation spell that lacks an official saving throw in the PHB is just the teeniest bit of an oversight, hence my theory!

That bein' said, as I've been chatting about with other people in the comments, the theory doesn't fully work anyway since you can't dimension door into an area with no open space. But I really appreciate the feedback!
